newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Most analysts anticipate carryover pressure in live cattle futures following last week's bearish USDA Cattle-on-Feed report and limit down close in October Monday. Much larger than expected placements and on-feed supplies at major feedlots and carryover technical fund liquidation were seen weighing on the market, analysts said.
Concern over the recall of Hudson Foods hamburger because of the possibility of E-coli contamination may again add to a bearish tone, they said.
However, some analysts consider the market oversold and also believe the public, in general, is not being swayed to stop buying hamburger by the recall of 1.2 million lbs of frozen beef patties.
Also, cash cattle could trade up $1 per cwt at $66 on this week's tighter feedlot showlists, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were seen under pressure on early indications for higher corn futures. This should prompt carryover selling and offset support from a higher CME feeder cattle index, analysts added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.13 at $81.00 per cwt.
